item.title: Callina Liang admitted that she felt a ton of pressure after she saw fans’ reactions to her getting cast as Chun-Li in the Street Fighter movie, specifically mentioning a thread she saw on Reddit.
item.description:
Callina Liang admitted that she felt a ton of pressure after she saw fans’ reactions to the news of her getting cast as Chun-Li in the Street Fighter movie, specifically mentioning a thread she saw on Reddit.
Yes, celebrities actually read what you say about them on the internet. Speaking with Project Big Screen, Liang revealed what went through her mind after she saw what fans were saying about her on Reddit when Deadline broke the news that she got cast as Chun-Li. And surprisingly, she has a lot more in common with the fighting game community than you might think.
“There was this Reddit thread: ‘Callina Liang’s thighs are nowhere as big as Chun-Li’s,’” she laughed. “But like, absolutely. When I look at it, as a huge fan myself, I would want whoever plays Chun-Li to be what I envision her to be in my head, and what you see of her in the video games and in the anime. She looks insane. Her body is insane.”
But Liang knew her limits. With just two months to prepare for the role, she didn’t have much time to grow her thighs as big as the First Lady of Fighting Games — but she was determined to do her best with the time she had, while making sure to be realistic about her goals.
“I did feel a lot of pressure. I was like, ‘Right, I gotta get my s**t together.’ My motto the whole time was just, ‘No regrets. Give it your all. It doesn’t matter how big you can physically get.’ You know, I only had two months. I had to be realistic with myself. I had to be a functioning human being who could act on screen at the end of the day. If I went full-throttle with building my body a certain way, I probably wouldn’t be able to function normally.
“I was just like, 'Have zero regrets, try your best and some, and whatever result you end up with, you can say, at least I gave it my all.' That’s what I did, and I think I'm happy.”
Photos taken from set prove that Liang’s efforts paid off. In fact, the actress revealed that she ate a dozen eggs every single day, as well as a meal every two hours, in order to meet her calorie goals and grow her muscles — to the point where she almost threw up. It worked, though, as she was able to grow her thighs 6.5 centimeters each. Even her stunt double couldn't keep up, who had to wear butt pads in order to realistically sell the idea that she and Liang were the same person in the film.
"Chun-Li is all kicks. So we did a bunch of Taekwondo training, Muay Thai, and Wushu (Kung Fu). I did two hours of that a day and strengthened my legs a lot and changed my diet drastically. When I was bulking, I ate 12 eggs a day. Every two hours I had to have a meal, and I was on the verge of throwing up. But it worked. By the end of the shoot, my thighs had grown six-and-a-half centimeters each,” she said in an August interview with Empire Magazine.
You can catch Liang’s martial arts skills firsthand in the Street Fighter movie, which releases in theaters this Friday, October 16.

item.title: Xbox has reportedly surveyed players on how they would feel about a return to console exclusivity for all of its games, with the exception of Call of Duty.
item.description:
Xbox has reportedly surveyed players on how they would feel about a return to console exclusivity for all of its games, with the exception of Call of Duty.
The survey, first spotted and shared by Windows Central, asks fans multiple questions about exclusivity. Some of these questions ask about specific games, such as Fallout, being exclusive to Xbox consoles and PC, while one question asks fans to imagine a world where all Xbox titles, excluding Call of Duty, were made exclusive to Xbox and PC. Interestingly, one question also suggests removing Minecraft from sale on platforms like PlayStation and Nintendo, though players who already own the game could keep it. However, existing Minecraft games would not receive any further updates.
"Imagine it was announced that all future title releases from every Xbox-developed gaming franchise except Call of Duty will be console-exclusive to Xbox," the question reads. "For Minecraft only, existing titles would no longer be available for purchase on PlayStation or Nintendo consoles, and would not receive any new content updates. However, there is no impact to any of the existing titles or content you already own. Nothing changes on PC in this announcement."
The survey's questions are largely trying to see if fans really care about exclusivity, if they would switch hardware for it, or if they would skip a game because it was made exclusive. Whether this will actually amount to anything remains to be seen; companies consider a wide range of possibilities, regardless of how realistic they may be. However, all of this suggests that Xbox is at least considering on doubling down on exclusivity.
Earlier this summer, Xbox announced that Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution would be exclusive to Xbox and PC forever, but were hesitant to confirm exclusivity for other titles. Games like Forza Horizon 6 and Fable are still slated to come to PS5, but it's unclear what will happen when something major like The Elder Scrolls 6 is released.
As of right now, we'll just have to wait and see what the future holds. Xbox is in a pretty critical spot right now, where it is trying desperately to salvage not only its reputation, but its financial viability after a tough generation. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reportedly pointed the finger at Game Pass in a recent meeting, as players were no longer incentivized to purchase major releases like Call of Duty on day one.
Xbox has spent this year walking back some of its previous plans by pulling Call of Duty from Game Pass on day one, and it's also rumored to be making some changes to day one offerings in 2027. It'll be interesting to see where Sharma takes Xbox next, but it does appear that they're trying to see what fans want before making some big changes.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: I got the chance to chat with the cast of the Street Fighter movie ahead of its theatrical release, and almost all of them are game for a crossover film with Mortal Kombat.
item.description:
I got the chance to chat with the cast of the Street Fighter movie ahead of its theatrical release, and almost all of them are game for a crossover film with Mortal Kombat.
In May 2026, Mortal Kombat co-creator Ed Boon posted about wanting a Street Fighter guest character in a Mortal Kombat game, saying he was a “huge fan” of Capcom’s flagship fighting game franchise.
Given that Mortal Kombat II released in theaters earlier this year, I had to ask the actors starring in the Street Fighter movie if they’d be willing to throw down with the likes of Shao Kahn to protect Earthrealm alongside Liu Kang and co. — and the consensus was a resounding “yes.”
In fact, Andrew Schulz joked that he was trying to make this collaboration happen with his viral joke at the 2025 Game Awards, where he famously took shots at the cast of Mortal Kombat II.
“This is what we were trying to do at [The Game Awards]!” Schulz told me. “We’re trying to set this thing up!”
“That’s what we were trying to do,” Cody Rhodes added.
“Tell them I know Noob Saibot which is [Ed Boon's and John Tobias’] names backwards,” Eric Andre interjected. “...but a crossover? A Flinstones/Jetsons crossover? We’re in. Let’s go.”
Andrew Koji, Noah Centineo, and Callina Liang were also enthusiastic about the idea. Koji specifically mentioned Marvel vs Capcom as another possible crossover opportunity… though the likelihood of this particular partnership happening is looking astronomically low.
“Hell yeah,” Koji said to the Mortal Kombat idea. “I said yes, because I’ve got friends in Mortal Kombat.”
“See, he’s got friends that worked on Mortal Kombat, so he’s trying to play nice over there,” Centineo joked.
“I love the girl who plays Kitana,” Liang said. “I’ve met Adeline a few times. She’s awesome.”
“That’d be sick,” Koji continued. “But then there’s Marvel vs Capcom. We’ve gotta tap into that.”
“I’m down for Marvel,” Liang agreed.
“Here’s what I want — I want more Street Fighter,” Centineo said. “If you bring an opportunity to us to be able to come back and reup these incredible characters, I’m down, and I know we’re all down. So if that’s Mortal Kombat, if that’s me kicking Thor in his face, you know?”
Of course, a Mortal Kombat x Street Fighter film might be a bit tricky, given that Mel Jarnson plays a character in both movies. I asked her about the possibility of such a project on the red carpet at the Street Fighter movie premier, and even though it’d be a bit of a challenge, she was more than willing to take on.
“It would be epic!” she said. “And you would bring Nitara back to life. Sew her back up. She’d be like half-blonde, with a wing. Half-Cammy, half-Nitara.”
For now, it remains to be seen if there’s real potential for a wacky crossover movie with these two fighting game series — but if the stars align, everyone seems pretty enthusiastic about it. And given both franchises’ wealth of guest characters and crossover games over the years, it wouldn’t exactly be uncharted territory.
Street Fighter releases in theaters on Friday, October 16, 2026.

item.title: The iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable, is already an incredibly expensive phone, rolling in at $1,999 to start. But, while the buy-in price is high, it's also going to be extremely expensive if it breaks.
item.description:
The iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable, is already an incredibly expensive phone, rolling in at $1,999 to start. While the buy-in price is high, it's also going to be extremely expensive if it breaks.
Ahead of the iPhone Duo's release next week, the foldable's repair costs were found by 9to5Mac, and they're staggering if you don't have AppleCare+. They range from damage on the glass back of the phone costing you $199 to inner screen damage costing $999 to repair. Apple will apparently also charge up to $1,499 to fix "other damage," though it's not clear what exactly that means.
All of these prices will be drastically lowered by having AppleCare+. Because the iPhone Duo is such an expensive and complicated device, anyone dropping the cash to buy one should seriously consider bundling AppleCare with it. I'd even go further and suggest picking up an iPhone Duo case on top of that.
As scary as these high repair prices look, Apple basically skipped the era of fragile foldables. Back when the first Samsung foldables were coming out, they were notoriously prone to damage, with displays that had gaps when folded, allowing particles of sand to get in there and wreak havoc on the inner screen. You could even peel the outer layer of the display off, a problem so bad that Samsung actually had to get around by putting out a statement telling people that the outer display layer was not a screen protector.
To Apple's credit, the iPhone Duo probably won't be quite as fragile as the foldables of yore, but it is still a phone with plenty of moving parts, which can always lead to unforseen damage. But we probably won't know exactly how durable it is until it actually makes its way into people's hands later this month. There's also a chance that the Duo's unique display aspect ratio will make it one of the first foldables that's actually good for gaming.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

The Pokémon Center just dropped its 2026 holiday collection, revealing this year’s theme as ‘Winter Night Sky.’
Like any TPC merch drop, the full list of 60+ new products is all over the place. The designs are generally unified by starry skies and pastel auroras, with new illustrations of Pokémon getting up to some festive activities.
The collection, which includes a mix of decor, apparel, and gift-wrapping accessories, is now available exclusively from The Pokémon Center. Any purchases from the collection before December 25 will come with a free Winter Night Sky sticker sheet, while supplies last.
The very literal star of the show is Mew, who made it to the big leagues as this year’s tree topper. The ethereal Pokémon is also getting a dedicated stocking, listed at $19.99.
Of course, this wouldn’t be a holiday collection without some new Pokémon decorations for your tree. New individual ornaments feature detailed holiday-themed models of Slowpoke, Amaura, Piplup, and a spread of Eeveelutions. The retailer also has new themed packs of standard round baubles.
If you’d rather have your beloved Pokemon firmly planted on a surface, TPC dropped three new additions to its Holiday Village figure collection: Town Hall Greetings, Meloetta Majestic Theatre, and Yamper Snowy Scamper.
On the apparel side, we’re seeing new sets of cozy pajamas as well as some t-shirts and knit beanies. Per Pokémon’s press release, “These cheerful cold-weather companions are ready to keep Trainers warm, cozy and full of wonder all winter long.”
There’s plenty more random things in the full collection. Again, the full list includes over 100 new products. A personal standout is the new 1,000-piece puzzle which features my beloved Piplup, but you’ll find everything from table runners and tea towels to snow globes and blankets.
I’m of the opinion that any of these would make great gifts. For what it’s worth, the collection also includes a ridiculous amount of gift boxes and bags that I would cherish just as much as whatever ends up being inside.
As for the trading card side of things? Well, we (at least some people) just got our hands on the 30th Anniversary set, and it remains to be seen whether we’ll be getting a 2026 edition of the TCG’s usual Holiday Calendar.
Too soon for holiday vibes? Check out the Halloween collection The Pokémon Center released earlier this month.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Andrew Schulz explained the viral moment when he called out the cast of the Mortal Kombat II movie, saying he was hoping for a 'Barbenheimer' moment and a possible collaboration between the two fighting game franchises.
item.description:
At the 2025 Game Awards, actor, comedian, and podcast host Andrew Schulz infamously called out the cast of the second Mortal Kombat movie while promoting the Street Fighter film, in which he stars as Dan Hibiki.
“We’re not the only game that appreciates your patronage,” Schulz said. "There's another game out there. They also flew from around the world to be here because they appreciate you. So give it up for the whole cast of Mortal Kombat 2!”
It turns out that the cast hadn’t actually shown up for the Game Awards, which Schulz capitalized on for his bit on stage. “Just kidding,” he continued. “They didn’t come. They don’t care about you, they only care about money, okay? We care about money and you! Street Fighter forever!”
The cast of the Street Fighter Movie just threw BIG shots at the Mortal Kombat Movie Kast at #TheGameAwards! Oh it's on! 😤 https://t.co/IbclswNMnq
Although his fellow cast members clarified that he was merely joking, Schulz’s callout went viral, with many fans feeling like this was an unfriendly jab at a fellow fighting game adaptation. Even actor Lewis Tan, who starred in the films, spoke about the ordeal, saying Schulz was the "last person that should be talking shit on that stage."
I got the chance to ask Schulz about this joke ahead of the Street Fighter movie’s release — and Schulz told me that he was merely trying to stoke the flames of a good-natured rivalry with the Mortal Kombat II cast in classic pro wrestling fashion.
“Guys, I thought we were in this together! In the wrestling business, this is called a ‘work,’ right?” Schulz began.
“Yep. You were workin’, they were shootin’,” Cody Rhodes confirmed.
“I read what was on the prompter,” Schulz continued. “...I thought that we were gonna turn into Barbenheimer. You know, rising tides lift all boats.”
“But you dissed them,” Eric Andre interjected.
“I got them a lot buzz,” Schulz countered.
“Here’s a follow-up,” Rhodes said, looking at me. “Do you have a Mortal Kombat tattoo?”
(I feel the need to explain; you might’ve seen the viral clip of this trio asking me to show them my M. Bison tattoo during this same interview. If not, you can watch it down below.)
“I do not,” I answered.
"Exactly,” Schulz said, to which Cody responded that he wasn’t “trying to fire another shot.”
“I was waiting for a thank you!” Schulz joked when I asked for his thoughts on the debate that his remarks had stirred up online. “You know, we used our platform to promote our movie to promote another movie! I feel like that's a very generous thing to do!”
Since we were on the topic of Mortal Kombat, I had to bring up the fact that the series’ co-creator, Ed Boon, recently expressed interest in a potential crossover game with Street Fighter. When asked if they’d be willing to star in a crossover film with the franchise, Schulz told me that was essentially what he was trying to accomplish with his viral callout at The Game Awards.
“This is what we were trying to do at [The Game Awards]!” Schulz said. “We’re trying to set this thing up!”
“That’s what we were trying to do,” Cody Rhodes added.
“Tell them I know Noob Saibot which is [Ed Boon's and John Tobias’] names backwards,” Eric Andre interjected. “...But a crossover? A Flinstones/Jetsons crossover? We’re in. Let’s go.”
(All three actors clarified that they have nothing but love for the Mortal Kombat franchise and the cast in the films; this hilarious trio was merely bantering with me about the situation, but it's clear they are definitely willing to work with the Mortal Kombat folks in some capacity.)
This was a sentiment echoed by most of the Street Fighter cast members that I interviewed. Almost every one of them were game for a possible collaboration with another fighting game franchise, with Andrew Koji and Callina Liang specifically mentioning Marvel vs Capcom.
However, director Kitao Sakurai has made it clear that any future Street Fighter films depend on how well the first one performs in theaters. Having seen it myself, I can say that it’s very good fun and full of lore and Easter eggs that fans will enjoy — but you’ll have to form your opinion when you sit down to watch it for yourself.
Street Fighter hits theaters on October 16, 2026.

item.title: Rockstar Games has revealed that it originally intended to develop GTA 6 alongside Red Dead Redemption 2, meaning it probably would've come out much sooner than we ever realized.
item.description:
Rockstar Games has revealed that it originally intended to develop GTA 6 alongside Red Dead Redemption 2, meaning it probably would've come out much sooner than we ever realized.
As told in a new article from Bloomberg, Rockstar Games initially planned to develop Red Dead 2 and GTA 6 at the same time, but that quickly became infeasible. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson recognized that the ambition behind Red Dead Redemption 2 meant they would need to treat it as an all-hands-on-deck situation, which also meant putting GTA 6 on the back burner. However, GTA 6 would benefit from this, as Nelson noted to Bloomberg that everything they built for Red Dead would "pay off" in GTA 6.
That appears to be true, as GTA 6 uses a lot of ideas and systems from Red Dead Redemption 2, including its NPC interaction system. It seems unlikely that GTA 6 would be what it is today if it had stayed the course and been developed in tandem with the western sequel. Unfortunately for fans, it means the game took much longer to make. Had it been developed simultaneously, it seems likely that Rockstar would've been able to release GTA 6 in the early 2020s.
Of course, the first release window that Rockstar ever actually publicly provided for GTA 6 was 2025. The game was delayed a couple of times, much to the bewilderment of Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive. Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe noted that she had to call Zelnick just months after announcing the game's first delay to inform him that they would need more time.
“I think he said, ‘You’re kidding. Please tell me you’re kidding,’” recalled Kolbe to Bloomberg. “But once we talked through why, he got it. And I think we are really lucky that he is as reasonable as he is, because a lot of people would say, ‘You’d just better figure out how to ship it.’ And we have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and we’ve all played those games. It’s not great.”
Bloomberg's report dispels rumors that GTA 6 has been in active development since shortly after GTA 5 was released in 2013, but that doesn't mean Rockstar only began working on it after Red Dead 2's launch. Various teams and leadership within Rockstar have been researching and planning GTA 6 since as early as 2014. Rockstar has spoken at length in recent interviews about taking staff to Florida to research and dream up ideas for GTA 6 during the mid to late 2010s.
Bloomberg noted that the team didn't have a "skeleton" for GTA 6's story until the end of 2019, a year after Red Dead 2's release. Even then, it took a while before the team was able to fully wrap its head around what the game would be. Rockstar has vowed to not take nearly as long on its next game, thanks to the fact it seems to have fewer obstacles going forward.
Rockstar doubled in size during GTA 6's development, encountered multiple leaks, had a loss in productivity during the pandemic, and much more. The studio also made major changes to how it operates and expects that will set it up for success moving forward. What is Rockstar's next game? We don't know. Some may expect Red Dead 3, but other fans are hoping that Rockstar will break the cycle of alternating between Red Dead and GTA in favor of something new or reviving a different IP. Whatever the case is, don't expect it to take another eight years.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: The Steam Frame came out a month ago, and while it is one of the best PCVR headsets, its lenses weren't quite as high-quality as some of its competitors. However, it seems like Valve might be working on a mid-generation refresh with OLED optics.
item.description:
The Steam Frame came out a month ago, and while it's one of the best PCVR headsets out there, its lenses weren't quite as high-quality as some of its competitors. However, it seems like Valve might be working on a mid-generation refresh with OLED optics.
According to SteamFrameHub, which dug through some of the source code for the Steam Frame kernel, the OS has references to a different Steam Frame with OLED optics, code named 'Plano.' Take this with a massive grain of salt, of course. But if it's real, the Plano headset would have largely the same specs as the existing Steam Frame, just with OLED panels with a per-eye resolution of 3,552x3,840, compared to the 2,160x2,160 pancake lenses found in the Steam Frame.
A higher-resolution OLED display would do wonders for the Steam Frame, especially for anyone using it for PCVR, rather than trying to play standalone games. Those better lenses would come a much higher price, though; as SteamFrameHub notes, the leaked optic specs line up nicely with the lenses found in the Samsung Galaxy XR headset, which starts for around $1,799. However, that headset launched before the RAM crisis kicked off, so a Steam Frame that matched its specs would likely be at least a bit more expensive.
Just like the rest of Valve's hardware this year, the Steam Frame was supposed to kick off a new era of accessible PC hardware, fueled by SteamOS at its center. However, because of an ongoing RAM crisis that won't be ending any time soon, the impact has been greatly diminished. Still, there are at least some people who seem to be buying the Steam Frame and the Steam Machine, as they're both still completely sold out at the time of writing.
Because Valve is still working on getting through the reservation list and waitlist for the Steam Fame, it's safe to assume that even if a Steam Frame OLED is a thing that will actually exist, it probably won't come out for quite a long time. The real question then, is whether or not that'll happen before Valve finds the perfect chipset that'll make the company want to make a Steam Deck 2. Just like with everything else Valve, we'll simply have to wait and see.

item.title: We got the chance to chat with Olivier Richters on the Street Fighter red carpet, who told us that he would love to play Tyr in Prime Video’s live-action God of War series.
item.description:
We got the chance to chat with Olivier Richters on the Street Fighter red carpet, who told us that he would love to play Tyr in Prime Video’s live-action God of War series.
Richters is a massive man. Standing over seven feet tall and weighing more than 350 pounds, it makes sense why he was cast as Zangief in the Street Fighter movie — and it’s also the reason why he wants to try his hand at playing Tyr.
In fact, he credits it for being the reason why he didn’t make the cut to play Kratos when Ryan Hurst, who was previously cast in the role, was forced to leave the project after sustaining a serious bicep injury while filming a stunt for the show.
“I think I can be open [about it],” he told us. “I did an audition. I really got high up the chain, even got two callbacks, and eventually they chose Dave Bautista. Much respect for him, he’s a great choice. Of course, in some universe if he didn’t exist, I would have loved to play the role. Maybe in the future.
“Every year I’m acting, I’m learning more and more. If I’m really honest, I think there’s one character who suits me better, and that’s Tyr. I would love to play him. I don’t know if he’s gonna be portrayed in the first season or second season, but my agent told them, ‘Olivier wants to be Tyr.’ So, let’s see if it happens.”
Richters mentioned this back in February on his Instagram account, showing himself decked out in a Kratos cosplay. “Realistically... at 7'2" / 2.18m, I might be too big for the role. I would literally tower over every other character. My real dream? A chance to audition for Týr. That would, in my opinion, be perfect,” he wrote.
While his future in the God of War show is currently unclear, he’s now reveling in the spotlight as Zangief in the new Street Fighter movie. In fact, he’s training in Street Fighter 6 right now with some seasoned pros with genuine hopes to be the “best” Zangief on all fronts — not just in the movies.
“I’m not lying — I’m really dedicated to becoming one of the best Zangiefs out there,” he revealed. “I’m not there yet, but I want to enter a tournament one time as the real Zangief playing Zangief. I just met a pro Zangief player, we spoke, and we’re gonna train together. If there is gonna be a second [movie], I want to be the ultimate Zangief.”
As a member of the fighting game community, I can definitely say that we welcome Richters into the fold with open arms and can’t wait to see him at a major someday. Maybe Evo 2027?

item.description:

Players - or Pissers, as they're called in the game - have to race around the map trying to golden shower items to claim them before anyone else can, like buildings, cars, and fountains, waggling their, um, appendages and generally causing chaos. If weaponized incontinence doesn't appeal to you, you can always play as the police hunting down the Pissers instead.

item.description:
Today IGN Fall Fan Fest 2026 shared a new sneak peek at How to Rob a Bank, the new upcoming heist movie starring Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz, Anna Sawai, Rhenzy Feliz, Christian Slater, with Pete Davidson and John C. Reilly.
The movie tells the story of a group of criminals with a thing for masks and mayhem who go viral sharing their heists on YouTube, but - perhaps not surprisingly - soon catch the attention of law enforcement. item.title: Atom Eve got a Casual costume in Invincible VS and, to no one’s surprise, the show’s fanbase is going feral for it.
item.description:
Atom Eve got a Casual costume in Invincible VS and, to no one’s surprise, the show’s fanbase is going feral for it.
If you’re familiar with Invincible at all, you’ve probably seen some discourse online surrounding Atom Eve’s weight gain in the show and comics. We won’t spoil anything for you in this article, but it’s a byproduct of a major story beat in the source material, and her transformation is often looked on fondly by fans — if not outright preferred over her slimmer design.
The devs at Skybound Games have been hard at work developing new characters and costumes for Invincible VS, the show’s tie-in 3v3 tag fighting game, most recently unveiling Angstrom Levy as a playable character… but the big brainiac isn’t who’s got players talking right now.
Alongside this character, Skybound also released a few alternate costumes for its other characters, including a ‘casual’ outfit for Atom Eve. And while she’s certainly dressed down, it’s her weight gain that’s got the fanbase in a tizzy.
It’s safe to say that everyone’s pretty thirsty for this particular version of Eve, with one excited player writing, “We ALL copping Everyday Eve, right?”
“Invincible better be able to fight,” another joked.
“The people yearn for thicc Eve,” yet another said.
A new Invincible VS Skin for every Casual Friday, Dressed Up Weekend, and Duct-Tape Wednesday. https://t.co/qxdCVwCWBA
Still others are pleasantly surprised that the devs at Skybound chose to go in this direction for Eve’s alternate costumes, given that body diversity isn’t something seen very often for female characters in fighting games (though this is a trend that’s changing in more recent releases, with Marisa in Street Fighter 6 being a good example).
Invincible VS is leaning into the memes with its costumes and characters lately; Skybound also gave Mark a Duct-Tape Man costume (leaning into a ‘superhero costume’ he made in his childhood) and even including Agent Spider as a playable fighter, a character who’s basically a riff on Marvel’s Spider-Man, for all intents and purposes.
Invincible VS released earlier this year. IGN scored the game a seven out of 10, with our reviewer Mitchell Saltzman saying its “hard hitting and fast paced 3v3 tag fighting is a gust of fresh air, especially for those who miss the two-way interactable combo system of Killer Instinct.”
The next season of Invincible is scheduled to release on Prime Video in early 2027. The show has been renewed for a sixth season, as well, becoming the platform’s longest-running animated series to date.

item.title: Watch the official IGN Fan Fest 2026 clip for Shudder's horror movie The Cycle, starring Deborah Ann Woll as a forensic anthropologist untangling a chilling cold case.
item.description:
Today at IGN Fall Fan Fest 2026 we got to see a clip from Shudder's new creepy crime thriller The Cycle, complete with an introduction from the movie's star (and the voice of Faye in the upcoming God of War Laufey), Deborah Ann Woll.
Woll plays Meg, a forensic anthropologist whose career takes a turn when her father's body turns up at a crime scene. Even more worryingly, that's one of the least weird things to happen in the movie, and without giving anything away, things go from police procedural to true supernatural spookiness in the best possible way. Horror author Stephen King even took to X to give it a shout-out.
"There's a movie coming on Shudder in October called THE CYCLE. I don't usually pump up horror movies (unless they are mine, haha), but this is special. Put it on your calendar."
It's written and directed by Jordan Downey, and you might have caught his work in V/H/S/Beyond, where he contributed Stork - a truly horrifying tale of a police unit investigating cases of missing babies - to the horror anthology series.
The Cycle will be released on Shudder on October 23.

item.title: Preorders are live for Microsoft's adorably tiny new Xbox Nano Controller.
item.description:
If you could use a smaller Xbox controller for any reason, Microsoft has announced just the thing for you. It’s called the Xbox Nano Controller, and it’s a more compact, more rectangular take on the standard Xbox controller. All the regular Xbox buttons are accounted for, but the form factor is smaller and more portable. It’s a nice-looking device overall, and it’s available to preorder now from a number of retailers (see it at Amazon). It will release on November 4 for $49.99.
Regular, full-sized Xbox controllers are nearly perfect, in my opinion. But I’m a grown man with large hands, and I almost never have to bring my Xbox controllers anywhere. If your hands are smaller, or if you travel with a controller on the regular, you might want something designed just for you. That’s the Nano controller.
It’s just over five inches long and weighs a mere 3.5 ounces. Microsoft says it supports “all 18 standard gameplay inputs,” which sounds like a lot. It also includes a rechargeable battery and a programmable Action Button (that little Tic—Tac-shaped button in the middle) that Microsoft says, “can be customized for features like screenshots, gameplay capture, and other frequently used shortcuts.” Pretty handy.
And thanks to its Xbox Wireless and Bluetooth capabilities, it works with all the same devices as a regular Xbox controller, including Xbox, PC, Mac, and mobile devices.
Where the standard Xbox controller has grips that fit larger hands comfortably, the Nano has grips that slide into your pocket comfortably. But the design looks comfortable, and I like the white-and-black color scheme, complete with colorful ABXY face buttons. The sticks look a little shorter than on the standard controller, but the disc-style D-pad looks the same. I'd like to try this thing.

item.title: Xbox controllers are already the default option for a whole range of devices, from the Xbox itself to gaming PCs and tablets. But Microsoft has just announced the Nano Controller, a smaller and cheaper Xbox controller.
item.description:
Xbox controllers are already the default option for a whole range of devices, from the Xbox itself to gaming PCs and tablets. But Microsoft has just announced the Nano Controller, a smaller and cheaper Xbox controller.
The Xbox Nano controller is essentially just a smaller Xbox Series X controller, and while Microsoft's blog doesn't share exact measurements, it is "about 5 inches" long and weighs 3.5 ounces, which is much smaller and lighter than the existing Xbox controller. The Nano Controller is also more affordable, coming in at $49.99, rather than the $69.99 that Microsoft typically charges for a controller. It's available to preorder now.
But while the Nano controller will be compatible with Xbox consoles, the focus here is on other devices like smart TVs, laptops, and any other device that, until recently, Microsoft would have claimed to be an Xbox. To that end, Microsoft is teaming up with Samsung to bundle the new Xbox Nano controller, along with two months of Game Pass with "select Samsung TVs" over the holiday season.
According to Microsoft's blog, the company is also working on a deal with Meta to include the Nano Controller, along with a Game Pass subscription to new Meta Quest owners, but it doesn't sound like that deal is quite set in stone. Still, Microsoft is targeting a holiday release for that, too.
Of course, the compatibility will stretch even further than just Samsung TVs and Meta Quest. Becuase the controller has both the standard Xbox wireless connection, along with Bluetooth, the Nano Controller should work with pretty much any device that supports Bluetooth. So, you could use this to play Fortnite on your iPad, if you're so inclined.
But while the Xbox Nano controller is Microsoft's first foray into mini controllers, it's far from an original concept. Companies like CRKD and 8BitDo have been selling mini controllers for years, and the selling point is the portability. With a controller this small, it's incredibly easy to slip it into a bag and take it wherever you go, without taking up too much space or adding a lot of heft to your bag.
This isn't the only thing that Microsoft's controller team has been working on. For months, there have been leaks suggesting that the new Xbox Elite Series 3 controller is right around the corner, and might even fix some of its predecessor's compatibility problems.
The Xbox Nano Controller will be available starting in November, and you can preorder it now. But as for the partnerships with Samsung and Meta, we'll likely just have to wait until those companies announce more details as the holiday season approaches.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

Apple recently announced a selection of new devices for your home that will be available in the coming weeks. These include the new Apple TV 4K with an A19 chip, the HomePod mini 2, and the brand-new Apple HomeView, which acts as a hub for your smart home devices. All the new Apple devices are up for preorder at Amazon and/or elsewhere. Let’s take a look.
Above, you'll find a cheat sheet of sorts for where to preorder these upcoming items. You'll find all of the retailer links below, along with details about each new item.
Apple’s one brand-new product in the recent announcement is Apple HomeView. It’s a Siri AI-equipped device with a screen and a speaker that you put in the kitchen or other central area in your household. It can have up to six users and can do a lot of different things, including manage your lights, doorbell, cameras, and other smart home devices (the full list of compatible items is here).
It can also access each user’s data to answer questions or pull up recipes or directions from your messages or maps app. It can do FaceTime calls and play music and all sorts of other things, too.
Apple HomeView is available to preorder now in four subtle color options for $299. You can get it with a stand to set on your counter, or without to be mounted on a wall. However, Amazon is already offering a discount, bringing select models down to $289.99.
The latest version of the Apple TV 4K runs on an A19 chip, which Apple says makes it up to 50% faster compared to the previous model. That means it’ll load your streaming apps faster and run Apple Arcade games better.
It also has Siri AI capabilities baked in (as long as you’ve paired the device with a recent iPad or iPhone). The new Apple TV has long-range microphones that let you talk to the digital assistant without having to press any buttons, which is pretty convenient. It costs $299 and is out November 13.
The HomePod mini 2 represents the first new hardware improvements on Apple’s smart speaker in six years. It looks similar to the previous model, but it packs the S10 chip, making it faster and more responsive. It also features Sound Glow lighting, Siri AI support (coming in a later update), and home theater capabilities. It’s not available for preorder on Amazon (yet?), but it’s available at all the other retailers.
Preorders for Apple's new folding phone aren't live yet (they start at 5 a.m. PT on Friday, October 16), but you can prepare your preorder now at Apple. You can sign in and make your selections, like color and storage size, as well as set up your trade-in, if applicable. Then, once preorders do go live, you'll be able to check out quickly.
Or, if you don't want to order directly from Apple, you can find links to your retailer of choice above.

item.title: Get an exclusive look at Johnny Depp's extensive makeup transformation into Ebenezer Scrooge for the upcoming film Ebenezer, plus a reveal of the brand-new movie poster.
item.description:
Johnny Depp’s take on the classic Christmas Carol story arrives next month, but we have an exclusive look at his transformation into the iconic Ebenezer Scrooge just in time for IGN Fan Fest.
Depp stars in the upcoming film Ebenezer and, as you can see in the exclusive video below, he underwent extensive makeup and prosthetic work for the role.
“I’ll be honest, the first time I saw him in full makeup I did not recognize him,” says Depp’s co-star Trammell Tillman, who plays the Ghost of Christmas Present. “Johnny was really excited to play Scrooge in his own way.
“Johnny really embraces the makeup process,” says Barrie Gower, Prosthetic Designer on the film. “He’s suggesting things like moles. He wanted his chin a little longer, anything that we can add to the character.”
In addition to a brand-new look at the movie, we can exclusively reveal a new poster for Ebenezer, which you can see below. The image showcases an up-close look at Depp’s Scrooge, along with Tillman’s Ghost of Christmas Present, the Ghost of Christmas Future (Robert Strange), and the Ghost of Christmas Past (Andrea Riseborough).
Depp’s co-stars on the film say the actor, known for transforming himself for roles like Pirates of the Caribbean’s Captain Jack Sparrow and Alice in Wonderland’s Mad Hatter, relished the opportunity to tackle character.
“I think he brings something unique to everything he does,” says Rupert Grint, who plays Bob Cratchit in the film. “I think this is such a perfect role for him.”
“Johnny is giving a performance the likes of which you’ve never seen before,” says Ian McKellen, who plays Marley. “But that’s what you expect with Johnny Depp, isn’t it? He’s full of surprises.”
“It’s Johnny doing what Johnny does best,” says Daisy Ridley, who plays Clara. “Which are these larger-than-life characters with a real human touch.”
Ebenezer arrives in theaters November 13.

item.title: Season 2 will arrive on Netflix in January 2027,
item.description:
Season 2 of Blue Eye Samurai is just around the corner and we have some major casting news just in time for IGN Fan Fest: Fall Edition. New episodes of the Netflix animated series drop soon, but you won’t have to wait that long for a brand new sneak peek of the show because IGN can exclusively reveal three new additions to the Blue Eye Samurai cast.
First, Joel Kim Booster will be joining the show as Priest Ando.
Next, here’s a look at Jonathan Pryce at Old Violet.
Finally, we can reveal the very first look at Sherry Cola as Kuma.
For the uninitiated, Blue Eye Samurai is Netflix's gloriously bloody animated revenge drama set in 17th century Japan. It follows Mizu (voiced by Maya Erskine), a swordmaster whose distinctive blue eyes make her an outcast. Disguised as a man and armed with a frankly inspiring talent for slicing and dicing her foes, Mizu embarks on a quest to hunt down the four white men who were illegally living in Japan at the time of her birth in an attempt to find her father. The first season ended with Mizu setting sail for London to continue her search, and we'll get to see what she finds in the city in season 2. I think we can safely assume it's not all going to be cups of tea and crumpets.
Created by Michael Green (his other works includes Logan and Blade Runner 2049) and Amber Noizumi, the series debuted in November 2023 and went on to grab an Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program, which is a respectable achievement for a show featuring so many severed limbs.
Season 2 will arrive on Netflix in January 2027. A third and final season is planned for 2028, marking an end to Mizu's journey.

item.title: Explore Jiaohun, a new Y2K-era psychological horror game from 12AM Blackout set in 1999 China where unfulfilled desires turn into terrifying inner demons.
item.description:
Calling all horror fans. Today IGN's Fall Fan Fest featured a new trailer for Jiaohun, a first-person psychological horror game set in a place in China called Fairy Town in Baishoi County, in 1999. Expect to encounter demons, secrets, and a nameless god among the abandoned buildings of the town.
The game references Chinese folktales and explores the concept of obsession through puzzles and exploration and is the work of developer 12AM Blackout. As well as hands with eyes, masked figures and unsettling imagery, players can enjoy encountering such mystical artifacts as… 1990's style pagers.
Jiaohun will launch for PlayStation 5 and PC via Steam in 2027. You can wishlist the game on Steam now.
